einstellungen.text: Ten minutes before your opening, the projector dies.
The picture shrinks to a white dot. The fan gets quieter. Then silent.
Ms. Sen presses every button she can find. Nothing. The screen stays black.
Out in the studio, a hundred and twenty guests are waiting. Parents, teachers, the whole grade. You hear shoes shuffling. Someone laughs.
Your hands are sweaty. Your whole presentation lives on that screen. Without it, you've got nothing. Or so you think.
"We push it back. Until it works again."
Three weeks of animations. Without the projector, they're nothing.
There it is again. The thought from the wall. And from the speech. You recognize it right away.
You've got the drawings. The yellow cards. Your sheet with the wrong word. Your dad's photos. Everything that's real.
Eda writes a sign. With a thick marker. You hang it on the door. You laugh for the first time today.
You carry everything up front. Cards, drawings, a roll of tape. Your hands aren't shaking quite as much.
You walk up to the mic without your perfect presentation.
